chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee', from Salih ibn Uqbah, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) who said:

"When you are under the Imams of injustice, proceed with their rulings and do not expose yourselves [to death], so that you may be killed. And if you act according to our rulings, that is better for you."

key_terms.أَحْكَامِنَا: Our rulings (referring to the Imam's rulings)
key_terms.أَحْكَامِهِمْ: Their rulings (referring to the unjust judges)

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia ruling on following current judges during the Imam's occultation?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* outlines the principle of *al-hukm bi-hukm al-adwal* (adjudicating by the rulings of the unjust rulers) during the Ghaybah, prioritizing political prudence and avoiding unnecessary martyrdom (*la tashharu anfusakum*) over strict adherence to Imamate law. It establishes a pragmatic legal framework where believers comply with the judicial decrees of contemporary authorities to maintain social order, while recognizing that applying the Imam’s specific jurisprudence remains spiritually superior when circumstances permit.
